Limping can lead to a stagnation of innovation, reduced productivity, and a decline in quality of life for many citizens. In the transport sector, limping can result in delayed and unreliable services, which can further exacerbate the problem by delaying essential services and infrastructure development.

Moreover, limping can lead to a lack of investment in infrastructure and technology, which can further hinder economic growth. The lack of support systems for those who experience limping can also hinder their ability to recover quickly from economic downturns. The cumulative effect of limping can lead to a cycle of poverty and stagnation, which can perpetuate a cycle of economic underdevelopment.
